title: One-scheme normalized coefficient Weil duality
statement: Fix $D,\ell,\Omega$ and a separated finite-type model $X_0$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. There exist actual finite/common coefficient duality data $B$ on its geometric fiber, with an internal-Hom identification and exceptional-unit dualizing identification [def-sf-common-stage-verdier-data], and a coefficient Weil-duality record $W$ [def-coef-verdier-weil-data] on this $B$, with its same evaluation and biduality, such that DualizingNormalization holds for $B,W$. In particular the finite scalar and finite-to-common dualizing and dual comparisons are equivariant. The duality is existential: the recorded interface pins the signed symmetry of the finite data only on literal K-flat pairs, so a duality whose biduality is twisted by a locally constant sign not preserved by geometric Frobenius (e.g. $X_0=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf F_{q^2}$) satisfies the interface but admits no Weil structure with equivariant biduality. This statement concerns one scheme and asserts no exceptional adjunction for a general relative morphism.

source.place: Proof paragraphs 1–3; One-scheme normalized coefficient Weil duality

proof.text: Construct $B$ with its internal-Hom and dualizing identifications by the normalized coefficient construction of [thm-coef-qbar-verdier], with the natural Koszul signed symmetry at every finite field. The Frobenius pullbacks are equivalences [lem-pod-isomorphism-field-transport]. At the structure morphism take the right mate of inverse canonical compact-support exchange [lem-coef-frobenius-exchange-equivalence, lem-weil-mate-iso-along-equivalences]. Apply it to the constant object with its tensor-unit identification, and conjugate by the given dualizing identification. Adjoint uniqueness makes it independent of compactification. The counit-normalized scalar comparisons give the dualizing scalar square.

Use the evaluation-normalized internal-Hom pullback comparison of [lem-pod-geometric-frobenius-internal-hom-comparison], conjugated through the given internal-Hom identification and the dualizing structure. On a Weil pair precompose its contravariant argument with the inverse structure. Naturality proves the arrow equation. Evaluation normalization gives the evaluation equation, and the injective tensor-Hom transpose of [lem-coef-completed-tensor-hom-transpose] applied after tensor symmetry gives the actual biduality square.

The finite scalar and common-stage comparisons are the evaluation-normalized comparisons of the same coefficient operations [thm-coef-rational-verdier, thm-coef-qbar-verdier]. Their two Frobenius routes have equal evaluation transposes, so they coincide. At common coefficients use the actual common-stage Hom and evaluation transport; finite representatives are an alternative verification by [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. No integral stable lattice is chosen.

lean.statement:
theorem coef_weil_normalized_duality
    (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (hl : l ≠ D.p)
    (Ω : Type v) [Field Ω] [Algebra (Padic l) Ω] [IsAlgClosure (Padic l) Ω]
    (X₀ : Over (Spec (.of D.k₀))) [LocallyOfFiniteType X₀.hom]
    [QuasiCompact X₀.hom] [IsSeparated X₀.hom] :
    ∃ B : CoefVerdierWeil.FiberDuality D l hl Ω X₀,
      Nonempty (CoefVerdierWeil.FiberInternalHom D l hl Ω X₀ B) ∧
      CoefVerdierWeil.FiberDualizing D l hl Ω X₀ B ∧
      ∃ W : CoefVerdierWeil.Coefficients D l hl Ω X₀ B,
        CoefVerdierWeil.DualizingNormalization D l hl Ω X₀ B W
